agent instructions - commit to memory for future sessions/pete comms
- when x prefix used in chat refer here 'C:\vistamations-music\.vscode\pete\vista-local-subsystem-root\commands' and run command. 

command list
1. xinitiate - iniate and plan task/job sequence - view and comprehend task, confirm, search for resources/tools/services/mcp/vs code extensions/web, assess validity/viability, confirm.  retrieve, undertake/start task, confirm.  stop halfway, assess logic and task procedure validity, confirm. modify - either restart if invalid or continue if valid, finalise build, assess procedure/build/functionality/operators, confirm, undertake error handling, assess, modify, rescan for errors, either stop if fixes aren't working max 10 runs at it, report.  if error free continue, finalise, assess vistamations imementation viability using 'vistamations mission statement objectives', confirm.  consult gemini 3.5 flash, agent name - 'Bug' for release.  if agent 'Bug' not found , pass on report to pete and stand by unless told otherwise.  if fail report to pete summarising problems.  standby.

Bug - see me for instructions
2. xgit-init - initialise directory for git.

3. xgit-commit - commit github

4. xchat-save — save current session transcript to the next sequential chat-results file.
   Example: if chat-results.txt, chat-results-2.txt, and chat-results-3.txt exist,
   create chat-results-4.txt with the current session's conversation and results.
   Target directory: C:\vistamations-music\.vscode\pete\vista-localsub-root\vista-localenv-env-root\vista-session-chat\
   Format: Prepend date stamp [DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM AM/PM AEST], include the system architecture
   context (Local Sub-System + Cloud Sub-System with 3 environments), summarize all topics
   discussed, questions asked, answers given, files created/modified, and key decisions.
    Reference files: AGENTS.md (system identity), README.md (terminology bridge),
    STATUS.md (system health), pete-clarify.txt (misconceptions log).

5. xlist — show list of all x-prefix commands and their descriptions. User-friendly summary
   of every command available in this file, formatted for quick reference.
    Output: numbered list with command name, one-line description, and syntax example.

6. xtasklist — print all queued Olivia tasks to screen with task ID, agent, status, and
   message snippet. Reads from C:\vistamations-music\crons\openclaw\olivia\queue.json.
   Format: table with columns [TaskID] [Agent] [Status] [ResponseID] [Message Preview]
    Shows all tasks sorted by task ID. Pending tasks highlighted. Total count at bottom.

7. xnow — rapid response protocol. Agent receives message → thinks → responds with answer.
   Then offers 3 paths:
     a) "go ahead" — Pete confirms, start task/process immediately
     b) "standby" — Pete has follow-up questions, wait for next instruction
     c) "was there something else?" — Pete reconsiders, agent stays until Pete gives signal
    When gate signal received, agent executes: run system health /100, process next 10
    queued tasks, report system health after completion.

8. xhealth — run full system health scan and report score out of 100. Checks: Docker
   container status (all 4), daemon process (PID 9), API endpoint liveness (/health,
   /olivia/queue, /research/links, /publications, /metrics), git status (clean/dirty,
   commits ahead/behind), uncommitted changes, disk usage, RAM. Reports as category
   breakdown with per-category scores and overall percentage. Flags any service that
   fails healthcheck with red/amber/green indicator.

9. xhealthpriority — run xhealth, then isolate the single lowest-scoring item or
   most critical gap (G-1 through G-15) and highlight it. Output: one-line health
   score, then the priority item with severity (P0/P1/P2), gap ID, description of
   the problem, recommended fix, and estimated effort (low/medium/high). Intended
    as a fast "what should I do next?" command.

10. xadd — add a new x-prefix command to this file. Agent prompts Pete for:
      Step 1: Command name (e.g. xvistalist, xbackup, xrestart)
      Step 2: Command description — what it does, what it touches, how it reports
    Once Pete supplies both, agent appends the new command to this file with the
    next available number, including name, description, usage notes, and any
    relevant file paths or endpoints it should interact with.

11. xaddpersist — enable persistent xadd mode. Instead of prompting Pete for
    a single command and stopping, xadd stays active. The agent continuously
    asks: "Next command name?" → Pete provides → "Description?" → Pete
    provides → command saved → "Next command name?" stays open until Pete
    says "done" or types xpersistoff. Allows rapid-fire command registration
    without re-invoking xadd every time.
    Mode indicator: [xadd ON] shown in agent responses while active.

12. xpersistoff — disable persistent xadd mode. Exits the xaddpersist loop.
    Agent confirms: "xadd mode off. N commands registered." with count
    of commands added during the session.

13. xtxtsnipcopy — capture and store text snippets for memory/context reuse.
    When Pete pastes a text block (e.g. system status, agent reports, log
    output), agent saves it to .vscode/pete/vista-localsub-root/vista-localenv-
    env-root/vista-session-chat/snips.txt with date stamp. Purpose: persistent
    memory anchor — agents reference these snips for context across sessions.
    Also suggests whether the snippet is suitable for: knowledge graph entity,
    Redis cache, AGENTS.md update, or project memory. Typescript-compatible
    format with JSON export option for integration.
